To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the scattering of light by a collection of small particles is orientation dependent and that, in the near and far field, the scattering can be enhanced or reduced depending on the orientation and the wavelength.

the scattering of light by a small, spherical, transparent particle embedded in an optically continuous medium depends on the particle size and shape, the spatial arrangement of the particle, and the wavelength and direction of the incident light.
the scattering of light by a small particle is influenced not only the bulk optical properties but also the shape and spatial arrangement of that particle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a theoretical framework to describe the optical properties of micro- and nanostructures, with the ultimate goal of predicting the optical response of a coating or a suspension based on its composition, microstructure, and processing history.
the optical properties of small particles embedded in continuous transparent media.

the scattering of light by randomly oriented, closely packed particles embedded in a transparent medium and the influence of particle interactions on the scattering efficiency and the spatial arrangement of the scattering intensity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multiple scattering is not always a good thing.

the orientation of the scattering particle(s) with respect to the direction of the incoming light is the most critical parameter in determining the magnitude of the scattering and that the spatial arrangement of the particle(s) has a secondary effect.
the scattering properties of a system of particles can be strongly influenced by their size, shape, orientation, and arrangement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the near-field effects are more complex than previously thought, and that the orientation and spatial arrangement of small particles in the near field can be used to tailor the optical properties of a coating or a stereolithographic suspension.
the scattering from small particles can be enhanced or diminished depending on the orientation and the spatial arrangement of the particle with respect to the incoming light.

the scattering efficiency and the spatial arrangement of the light scattered from a collection of particles are strongly orientation-dependent and can be significantly different from those of a single particle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orientation dependence of near-field scattering from small particles can have important consequences for a variety of applications.

, in addition to the bulk optical properties and microstructure of a medium, the spatial arrangement of particles within that microstructure is important to the magnitude and spatial distribution of the light scattered in the near and far fields.
the orientation of the scattering particles relative to the incident light can have a large influence on scattering, which should be considered when designing materials and devices.
